A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PATRA research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including material moved between appendices and the main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original TSQA and MTBench evaluations, ablations, a synthetic latent-decomposition analysis, and downstream forecasting, anomaly-detection, and classification results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluated baselines to the TSQA and MTBench comparisons.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 retain the same latent decomposition, learnable alignment tokens, attention-based fusion, supervised alignment stage, GRPO training, and balanced reward functions. No algorithmic or architectural change is documented.

E1.justification: Coverage remains the four TSQA task categories, MTBench weather and finance tasks, the synthetic decomposition scenario, and common forecasting, anomaly-detection, and classification tasks. The downstream evaluations move from Appendix I to Appendix G without changing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated TimeOmni-1-7B and ITFormer-7B baselines. Table 2 adds both models plus GPT-5.2 and Gemini-3-Pro, substantially broadening the comparisons with specialized time-series methods and proprietary models. Existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: The stated 90/10 TSQA split, task metrics, standardized prompts, deterministic decoding, and weather/finance training exclusions remain unchanged. The additional baseline comparisons introduce no documented revision to these protocols.

E4.justification: Component ablations, tuned-versus-zero-shot comparisons, reward balancing, training curves, success/failure cases, and latent-decomposition analysis are retained. Sections 5.9–5.10 relocate analyses already present in v1 Appendices E and G; the failure case also moves into Section 5.8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Deterministic decoding, training-reward smoothing, and the correlation-reporting practice in the decomposition analysis are unchanged.

E6.justification: New baseline results substantially extend Tables 1–2 and alter comparative rankings. TimeOmni-1 reaches 42.56% TSQA reasoning accuracy versus PATRA's 44.59%; ITFormer achieves better 7-day finance MSE, 0.174 versus PATRA's 0.191. Previously reported scores, including PATRA's and the appendix results, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The task formalization and mathematical definitions in Equations 1–14 are retained. Neither version adds or removes theoretical assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about pattern-aware alignment, balanced reinforcement learning, superior TSQA performance, and generalization. Additional comparator evidence does not introduce a new core claim.

C2.justification: v1 Appendix F explicitly connects the failure case to local salient features overriding global direction and suggests stronger regularization for low-signal-to-noise sequences. v2 Section 5.8 retains the attention-bias explanation but omits that specific implication and proposed remedy.

D1.justification: v2 adds a PATRA GitHub repository link below the abstract, providing code-access information absent from v1. The PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or availability. Backbone, hardware, prompts, and disclosed reward settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v1's short Appendix H becomes a substantially expanded Appendix F discussing reasoning versus forecasting, missing data and distribution shifts, graph/hypergraph methods, anomaly prediction, and broader multimodal learning. Numerous distinct works are added and several earlier references removed, beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The revision makes localized structural changes: appendix discussions move into Sections 5.8–5.10, related-work prose is expanded, and acknowledgements, an impact statement, and authorship notes are added. The introduction, methodology, and conclusion remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain baseline rows, and table shading and highlighting are revised. The existing reward-ablation table, failure-case figure, and decomposition figure move into the main text. The underlying diagrams, plotted analyses, and prompt illustrations are retained.

improvement.justification: The broader comparisons in Tables 1–2 make the empirical assessment more informative, and the repository link improves access information. Existing diagnostic evidence is also easier to find in the main text. These gains are tempered by shortened limitation discussion and an unrevised Section 5.5 claim of leading all finance metrics, now contradicted by ITFormer's 0.174 MSE versus PATRA's 0.191.
